title: Hotelling’s T²: multivariate mean testing and the F transformation
objectives: Explain why Hotelling’s T² extends the one-sample t test to a vector mean.
Compute the sample mean vector, unbiased covariance matrix and its inverse.
Evaluate T²=n(x̄−μ₀)′S⁻¹(x̄−μ₀) without losing cross-product terms.
Convert one-sample T² to an exact F statistic and identify both degrees of freedom.
Distinguish one-sample, paired and two-sample Hotelling procedures.

prereq.name: Sample mean vector and covariance matrix
prereq.why: The statistic compares the observed mean vector with a hypothesised vector and scales the difference by sample covariance.

prereq.name: Matrix inverse and quadratic forms
prereq.why: The Mahalanobis quadratic form d′S⁻¹d accounts for variances and covariances jointly.

prereq.name: Student t and F distributions
prereq.why: The exact finite-sample test is conducted through an F transformation with specified degrees of freedom.

traps: For the one-sample statistic, use T²=n d′S⁻¹d; do not omit n.
Use the sample covariance with divisor n−1, not the maximum-likelihood divisor n, in the standard test.
The inverse covariance matrix is essential; separate univariate t statistics do not reproduce the joint test.
For one sample, F=(n−p)T²/[p(n−1)] with df (p,n−p).
For paired data, form difference vectors and apply the one-sample procedure.
Do not confuse the one-sample and pooled two-sample F transformations.

sheet: One-sample: T² = n(x̄−μ₀)′S⁻¹(x̄−μ₀), where S uses divisor n−1.
Let d=x̄−μ₀. Compute S, invert S, then calculate the full quadratic form d′S⁻¹d.
Under H₀ and multivariate normality: [(n−p)/(p(n−1))]T² ~ F(p,n−p).
Decision: reject H₀ when F exceeds the upper α critical value Fα;p,n−p.
Paired test: calculate each difference vector, then use the one-sample T² test on those differences.
Two independent samples with common covariance use pooled Sp and a different scaling and degrees-of-freedom formula.
S must be nonsingular; in particular, the sample size and data rank must support inversion.
tricks: Write p and n beside the formula before substituting; this prevents swapping degrees of freedom.
For a 2×2 symmetric matrix [[a,b],[b,c]], inverse is 1/(ac−b²)[[c,−b],[−b,a]].
Compute d′S⁻¹d as a matrix product in two stages and retain the off-diagonal terms.
shortcuts: Check S is symmetric and positive definite before inversion.
Check determinant ac−b² is positive for a positive-definite 2×2 covariance matrix.
If the question asks for T², stop at T²; apply the F conversion only when testing.
remember: T² is a squared multivariate distance, not itself an F statistic.
One-sample F degrees of freedom are (p,n−p).

howto: Work through the June 2026 question first, then derive the statistic from the geometry of a vector mean. The central calculation is the covariance-adjusted squared distance between x̄ and μ₀. The lesson separates computing T² from converting it to F, because examination questions may ask for either quantity. The paired and two-sample sections prevent formula transfer across designs.

scenes.title: The vector problem behind the test
scenes.objective: Recover the matrix ingredients needed for multivariate inference.
body: A univariate test asks whether one population mean equals a stated value. A multivariate test asks whether several population means, considered together, equal a stated vector.
The variables may be correlated. Testing each coordinate separately ignores that relationship and creates a different testing problem.
Hotelling’s T² measures how far the sample mean vector lies from the null vector after adjusting for the covariance structure.

items.ask: What does the diagonal of a sample covariance matrix contain?
refresh: The diagonal entry Sⱼⱼ is the sample variance of variable j. The off-diagonal entry Sⱼₖ is the sample covariance between variables j and k.

The off-diagonal terms matter because a displacement in one coordinate may be less unusual when it follows a direction of strong positive covariance. The inverse covariance matrix adjusts for that joint geometry.

items.ask: What is a quadratic form d′Ad?
items.recall: A scalar formed by multiplying a vector, a matrix and the vector transpose.
refresh: For a column vector d, d′Ad is a single number. If A is positive definite, it is non-negative and is positive for every non-zero d.
In Hotelling’s statistic, A=S⁻¹. The quadratic form measures squared distance after scaling and rotating according to the sample covariance.

items.ask: Which divisor defines the usual unbiased sample covariance?
refresh: The usual sample covariance matrix is the sum of outer products (xᵢ−x̄)(xᵢ−x̄)′ divided by n−1.
Using n instead changes S and therefore changes T². Keep the convention fixed throughout the calculation.

ask.q: Why is the covariance matrix needed rather than only the sample variances?
ask.nudge: Think about how correlated coordinates change the direction and scale of a displacement.

scenes.title: Distance that respects correlation
scenes.objective: Interpret T² as a covariance-adjusted distance.
body: Suppose a sample mean is two units above the target on variable 1 and one unit below on variable 2. Whether that displacement is unusual depends on the variables’ scales and their correlation.
Euclidean distance treats every direction equally. Mahalanobis distance rescales and rotates the displacement using the inverse covariance matrix.
Hotelling’s T² is n times the squared Mahalanobis distance between the sample mean and the hypothesised mean.

scenario.title: A manufacturing process
body: A plant monitors tensile strength and elongation. Historical measurements show positive covariance: batches with higher tensile strength often have higher elongation. A new sample mean is displaced from the target in both coordinates. The quality team wants one joint test rather than two isolated tests. The covariance-adjusted distance recognises that a displacement along the usual joint movement direction is less surprising than an equally long displacement against that pattern.
scenario.q: What feature makes the joint distance different from ordinary Euclidean distance?
scenario.answer: It uses S inverse, so it adjusts for both the variances and the covariance.

ask.q: What is the one-sample statistic proportional to?
ask.nudge: It is a sample-size multiple of a squared Mahalanobis distance.

scenes.title: Definition and exact F conversion
scenes.objective: State the one-sample statistic and its null distribution.

blocks.body: Let X₁,…,Xₙ be independent observations from a p-variate normal population with mean μ and nonsingular covariance Σ. Test H₀: μ=μ₀.
Under H₀: [(n−p)/(p(n−1))]T² follows F with p and n−p degrees of freedom.
The standard exact result assumes independent multivariate-normal observations and a nonsingular sample covariance matrix. The test is not distribution-free.

ask.q: For p=2 and n=10, what are the F degrees of freedom?
ask.nudge: The first is p; the second is n−p.

scenes.title: June 2026 Paper 2 Q4 — full calculation
scenes.objective: Reproduce the official T² value without skipping matrix arithmetic.
scenes.problem: Test H₀: μ=(3.5,2.5)′ from X₁=(1,2)′, X₂=(4,4)′ and X₃=(4,3)′. Find T².

steps.say: Compute the sample mean coordinate by coordinate.
steps.why: The three vectors contribute to each coordinate separately.
Keep the signs; the cross-product term depends on them.

steps.say: Compute the unbiased sample covariance matrix.
steps.why: The divisor is n−1=2. The off-diagonal sample covariance is 1.5.
Both diagonal and off-diagonal contributions are included.
The question asks for T² itself, not its F transform.

ask.q: What is the exact T² answer and the corresponding option?
ask.nudge: Multiply the quadratic form by n only after evaluating it.

scenes.title: Complete the F conversion
scenes.objective: Move from a computed T² to the correct F statistic.
scenes.problem: A one-sample test has p=2, n=8 and observed T²=12. Complete the conversion.

steps.why: Substitute p and n before simplifying.
This is the transformed test statistic.
The numerator df is p and denominator df is n−p.

scenes.after: Compare F=5.143 with the upper-tail critical value Fα;2,6. Do not compare T² directly with an F critical value.

ask.q: Why is it not enough to compare T²=12 directly with an F critical value?
ask.nudge: The two statistics have different null distributions and scales.

scenes.title: Design determines the formula
scenes.objective: Choose the correct Hotelling procedure for the sampling design.

blocks.body: For paired multivariate measurements, form Dᵢ=Xᵢ−Yᵢ for each pair. Test the mean difference vector with the one-sample Hotelling statistic.
With common covariance, pooled Sp and N=n₁+n₂: T²=[n₁n₂/N](x̄₁−x̄₂)′Sp⁻¹(x̄₁−x̄₂). The exact F conversion is [(N−p−1)/(p(N−2))]T² ~ F(p,N−p−1).
The two-sample formula has a pooled covariance and different scaling and degrees of freedom. It is not the one-sample formula with n replaced by N.
Independent groups, multivariate normality within groups and a common population covariance matrix underpin the classical pooled two-sample test.

ask.q: How do you handle a paired multivariate design?
ask.nudge: Reduce each pair to one difference vector.

scenes.title: Guided transfer: a paired process study
scenes.objective: Recognise and set up a paired Hotelling test.
scenes.problem: Five machines are measured before and after calibration on two performance variables. The research question is whether the mean change vector is zero. State the correct test statistic and F degrees of freedom; do not calculate a numeric result.
hints: The measurements are paired, so preserve each machine’s before-after link.
Create one two-dimensional difference vector per machine and use the one-sample procedure.
Here n=5 and p=2. Substitute these into the one-sample F conversion.
scenes.answer: Use Dᵢ=Afterᵢ−Beforeᵢ, then T²=5 D̄′S_D⁻¹D̄. The F transformation is (3/8)T² with df (2,3).
scenes.check: The denominator degrees of freedom are n−p=3.

solution.why: Pairing removes between-machine baseline variation from the target comparison.

solution.say: Treat the five difference vectors as one sample.
solution.why: There are n=5 vectors and p=2 response variables.
This is the one-sample transformation applied to the differences.

scenario.teaser: Repeated measurements on the same units.
scenario.title: Calibration before and after
body: Each of five machines contributes a pair of two-variable measurements: one vector before calibration and one vector after calibration. The two observations from the same machine are related, so the analysis must preserve that pairing. Treating the ten vectors as if they came from ten unrelated machines would discard the within-machine comparison and answer a different question.

The research question is whether calibration produces a non-zero average change in the two performance variables considered jointly. For each machine, subtract its before vector from its after vector. This creates five difference vectors in two dimensions. The null hypothesis is that the population mean of these difference vectors is the zero vector.

Now the dataset has the exact structure of a one-sample multivariate mean problem. Compute the mean difference vector and its sample covariance matrix, then apply the one-sample Hotelling statistic with n=5 and p=2. The F transformation therefore uses numerator degrees of freedom 2 and denominator degrees of freedom 3. This is a joint test; it does not say that each individual variable must change significantly on its own.
scenario.q: Why should the paired observations not be analysed as two unrelated samples?
scenario.answer: Because the two measurements from each machine are dependent and the pairing is part of the design.

ask.q: What is the denominator degree of freedom in the F conversion?
ask.nudge: Use n−p with n=5 and p=2.

scenes.title: Check the mistakes that change the answer
scenes.objective: Detect formula and design errors before submission.
scenes.intro: Mark each claim true or false and read the reason.

items.claim: The one-sample statistic is d′S⁻¹d without a sample-size multiplier.
items.why: The standard one-sample definition includes n: T²=n d′S⁻¹d.

items.claim: The sample covariance matrix in the standard test uses divisor n−1.
items.why: This is the unbiased sample covariance convention used in the exact formula.

items.claim: For a paired test, calculate differences and use the one-sample procedure.
items.why: The paired differences form one sample of p-dimensional vectors.

items.claim: For a one-sample test, the F degrees of freedom are (n−p,p).
items.why: The correct order is numerator p and denominator n−p.

ask.q: Which single omission most directly changes the June 2026 answer?
ask.nudge: Check the definition of T² after evaluating the quadratic form.

scenes.title: Transfer: calculate a simple two-dimensional T²
scenes.objective: Evaluate a covariance-adjusted distance with a diagonal covariance matrix.
scenes.problem: Let n=6, d=(1,−1)′ and S=diag(4,1). Find T².
hints: A diagonal matrix is inverted by taking reciprocals of its diagonal entries.
Multiply S⁻¹ by d before taking the dot product with d.
Then multiply the quadratic form by n.
scenes.check: The quadratic form is positive and equals 1.25.

solution.why: The inverse of a nonsingular diagonal matrix has reciprocal diagonal entries.
The sample-size multiplier belongs to the one-sample definition.

ask.q: What would T² be if the first variance were 1 instead of 4?
ask.nudge: The first coordinate would then contribute 1 rather than 1/4.

scenes.title: The complete exam routine
scenes.objective: Consolidate the calculation and design checks.
body: First identify the design: one sample, paired sample, or two independent samples. Choose the matching statistic before calculating.
For one sample, compute x̄, S with divisor n−1, d=x̄−μ₀, and S⁻¹. Then evaluate T²=n d′S⁻¹d.
If a hypothesis test is requested, convert to F using [(n−p)/(p(n−1))]T² and degrees of freedom (p,n−p).
For June 2026 Q4, T²=7.0 is option C. Its F equivalent is 1.75 with df (2,1). The requested answer was T², so option C is the response.
Before submitting, check matrix symmetry, determinant, signs in d, the n multiplier, and the order of the F degrees of freedom.

ask.q: State the one-sample formula and the F degrees of freedom from memory.
ask.nudge: Write T² first, then the conversion on a separate line.
